cues.en: Everyone,
cues.zh: 大家好，

cues.en: please think of your biggest personal goal.
cues.zh: 请想想你个人最大的目标。

cues.en: Okay? For real. You could take a second, you gotta feel this to learn it. Take a few seconds and think of your personal biggest goal. Okay?
cues.zh: 好吗？认真的。你可以花一秒钟，得真切感受才能学会。花几秒钟想想你个人最大的目标。好吗？

cues.en: Imagine deciding right now that you're going to do it. Imagine telling someone that you meet today what you're going to do. Imagine their congratulations
cues.zh: 想象现在就决定要去做。想象告诉今天遇到的某个人你要做什么。想象他们的祝贺

cues.en: in their high image of you. Doesn't it feel good to say it out loud? Don't you feel one step closer already like it's already becoming part of your identity?
cues.zh: 以及他们对你的高度评价。大声说出来是不是感觉很好？你是不是已经感觉更近一步了，好像它已经成为你身份的一部分？

cues.en: Well,
cues.zh: 嗯，

cues.en: bad news,
cues.zh: 坏消息是，

cues.en: you should have kept your mouth shut because that good feeling now will make you less likely to do it.
cues.zh: 你本该闭口不谈，因为现在这种良好感觉反而会让你更不可能去做。

cues.en: The repeated psychology tests have proven that telling someone your goal makes it less likely to happen.
cues.zh: 反复的心理学测试已经证明，告诉别人你的目标反而会让它更不可能实现。

cues.en: Anytime you have a goal, there are some steps that need to be done, some work that needs to be done in order to achieve it. Ideally, you would not be satisfied until you'd actually done the work. But when you tell someone your goal and they acknowledge it, psychologists have found that it's called a social reality. The mind is kind of tricked into feeling that it's already done.
cues.zh: 每当你有一个目标，总有一些步骤需要完成，一些工作需要在实现它之前去做。理想情况下，在真正完成工作之前你不会满足。但当你告诉别人你的目标并且他们认可了它，心理学家发现这叫做社会现实。大脑有点被欺骗，感觉它已经完成了。

cues.en: And then because you felt that satisfaction,
cues.zh: 然后因为你感受到了那种满足感，

cues.en: you're less motivated to do the actual hard work necessary.
cues.zh: 你就不那么有动力去做真正必要的艰苦工作了。

cues.en: So this goes against the conventional wisdom that we should tell our friends our goals. Right? So they hold it to it. Hold us to it. Yeah. So let's
cues.zh: 所以这与我们应该告诉朋友我们目标的传统观念相悖。对吧？这样他们就能监督它。监督我们。是的。那么让我们

cues.en: look at the proof. 1926,
cues.zh: 看看证据。1926年，

cues.en: Kurt Lewin, founder of social psychology called this substitution.
cues.zh: 社会心理学创始人库尔特·勒温称之为替代。

cues.en: Vera Mahler found when it was acknowledged by others, it felt real in the mind. 1982,
cues.zh: Vera Mahler 发现，当目标被他人认可时，人在心理上会觉得它已经成真。1982 年，

cues.en: Peter Goblitzer wrote a whole book about this, and in 2009,
cues.zh: Peter Goblitzer 为此写了一整本书，到了 2009 年，

cues.en: he did some, new tests that were published. It goes like this. A 163
cues.zh: 他又做了一些新测试并发表了。事情是这样的：有 163

cues.en: people across four separate tests.
cues.zh: 人，分布在四项独立测试中。

cues.en: Everyone wrote down their personal goal, then half of them announced their commitment to this goal to the room, and half didn't.
cues.zh: 每个人都写下自己的个人目标，然后一半人向在场的人宣布了自己对这个目标的承诺，另一半没有。

cues.en: And then everyone was given forty five minutes of work that would directly lead them towards their goal, but they were told that they could stop at any time.
cues.zh: 然后每个人都被给予 45 分钟的工作，这些工作会直接帮助他们朝目标前进，但他们被告知可以随时停下。

cues.en: Now those who kept their mouth shut worked the entire forty five minutes on average, and when asked afterwards said that they felt that they had a long way to go to achieve their goal.
cues.zh: 那些闭口不谈的人平均整整工作了 45 分钟，事后被问到时说，他们觉得自己离实现目标还有很长的路要走。

cues.en: But those who had announced it quit after only thirty three minutes on average and when asked afterwards
cues.zh: 但那些宣布了目标的人平均只工作了 33 分钟就放弃了，事后被问到时

cues.en: said that they felt much closer to achieving their goal.
cues.zh: 说他们觉得自己离实现目标近多了。

cues.en: So if this is true, what can we do?
cues.zh: 所以，如果这是真的，我们能做什么？

cues.en: Well, you could resist the temptation to announce your goal,
cues.zh: 嗯，你可以抵制住宣布目标的诱惑，

cues.en: you can delay the gratification that the social acknowledgement brings,
cues.zh: 你可以推迟社会认可带来的满足感，

cues.en: and you can understand that your mind mistakes the talking for the doing.
cues.zh: 并且你可以明白，你的大脑把“说”误当成了“做”。

cues.en: But if you do need to talk about something, you can state it in a way that gives you no satisfaction.
cues.zh: 但如果你确实需要谈某件事，你可以用一种不会让你产生满足感的方式来陈述它。

cues.en: Such as, I really want to run this marathon, so I need to train five times a week and kick my ass if I don't. Okay?
cues.zh: 比如：我真的很想跑这场马拉松，所以我每周得训练五次，要是没做到，就狠狠逼自己。好吗？

cues.en: So audience, next time you're tempted to tell someone your goal, what will you say?
cues.zh: 那么各位，下次当你忍不住想告诉别人你的目标时，你会怎么说？

cues.en: Exactly.
cues.zh: 没错。

cues.en: Well done.
cues.zh: 干得漂亮。

cues.en: Oh, very funny.
cues.zh: 呵，真逗。

cues.en: You got me.
cues.zh: 被你发现了。

cues.en: Changed it.
cues.zh: 已经改了。

cues.en: I changed it to a plus.
cues.zh: 我把它改成加号了。

cues.zh: 我们是 Intel。

cues.zh: 领创
